Two small asks so we can release invoices:

If you don’t have marketplace language on the standard resale cert, a short statement from your tax team confirming AWS is authorized to purchase on your behalf (and the FEIN/legal entity name) will work for our records.

I’ve cc'd Monica from Finance to help triage. We’re aiming to clear the hold this week.

Elena / Mallory team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — appreciate the AWS invoice sample. A couple of clarifying items from Redwood Finance so we can mark the account as exempt for the relevant transactions:

1) Legal entity name and FEIN: we have Mallory Tech, Inc. / FEIN 12-3456789 — can you confirm that is the legal entity that should appear on the resale certificate?
2) Certificate coverage: Tennessee generally accepts resale certificates for purchases where the buyer is the purchaser of record. For marketplace transactions where AWS is seller-of-record, Redwood’s policy is to accept either: (a) a resale certificate that explicitly references marketplace/reseller purchases, or (b) an invoice from AWS showing Mallory Tech as the underlying purchaser + an authorization statement from Mallory confirming AWS acts on your behalf.
3) Stamped copy: for our audit file we prefer a stamped or otherwise signed copy with a clear issue date.

If you can provide the stamped certificate and a one-line statement confirming the legal entity (per #1) we can clear the hold. If you prefer, Marcus (cc'd) can accept a DocuSign trail for the marketplace affidavit; I’ve included a template link in the next note.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Quick follow-up from Sales Ops: good work getting the signed certificate over. For internal clarity and to avoid future invoice holds, two acceptance paths we use for marketplace-heavy sellers:

Option A (preferred): Stamped resale certificate that contains blanket language covering purchases made through third-party marketplaces (e.g., "This certificate applies to purchases made through authorized marketplaces where the marketplace is the seller-of-record on the invoice"). If Mallory can provide that language on the certificate, we'll mark all existing Marketplace-era invoices as exempt in TN.

Option B: If certificate language cannot be amended, provide: (1) an AWS invoice showing Mallory as the buyer (you did), (2) a brief notarized/DocuSigned Marketplace Authorization (one-paragraph) confirming AWS invoices on your behalf for Mallory purchases, and (3) FEIN + legal entity confirmation.

I’ve uploaded our marketplace affidavit template here: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234 and attached a brief guidance PDF for your tax team. Once we receive the stamped certificate or the completed DocuSign affidavit we can release the invoice hold.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sales Operations
marcus_lin@redwood.com
